citations.title: Alternative Fuels Data Center: Emissions from Electric Vehicles
https://afdc.energy.gov/vehicles/electric-emissions

claims.text: All-electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids, and hybrids generally produce lower tailpipe emissions than conventional vehicles, with all-electric vehicles producing zero tailpipe emissions when operating on electricity.
A complete cradle-to-grave assessment of vehicle emissions must combine fuel-cycle (well-to-wheels) emissions with vehicle-cycle emissions from material production, manufacturing, and end-of-life.

The magnitude of the life-cycle emissions advantage of electric vehicles over gasoline vehicles depends heavily on the carbon intensity of the local electricity grid: low-carbon grids yield a large advantage while higher-emissions electricity generation reduces the benefit.

The IEA Global EV Outlook 2024 includes analysis of the life-cycle emissions of electric cars and their batteries, reflecting that lifecycle emissions is a central topic in authoritative global electric mobility assessments.
